issues.legal_issue: An appellate court cannot reverse a trial court’s decision by relying on a case that was neither pleaded nor made an issue between the parties.
material_facts: The plaintiffs pleaded that the deceased owned the restaurant and had employed the defendant, and that the defendant received possession on an assurance that he would manage it for them.
The defendant pleaded that he had always owned the restaurant.
The plaintiffs did not plead that the restaurant was a benami business, and the parties did not join issue on that theory.
The High Court reversed the trial court’s decision for the defendant on the basis that the restaurant was benami for the deceased.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment and decree were set aside, and the trial court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A case must be decided on the case pleaded by the parties, and a decision cannot rest on grounds outside their pleadings. The Court relied on Trejan and Co. Ltd. v. P.W. N.H. Nagappa Chettiar (1956) SCR 789 and Baraba Singh v. Achal Singh, AIR 1961 SC 1097.

rule.if: civil_appeal and appellate_court_reversed_trial_decree and appellate_court_relied_on_unpleaded_case and parties_did_not_join_issue_on_that_case

predicates.civil_appeal: A party brought a civil appeal challenging a decision made by a trial court.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_trial_decree: The appellate court reversed the trial court’s decree.
predicates.appellate_court_relied_on_unpleaded_case: The appellate court relied on a factual or legal case that was not pleaded by the parties.
predicates.parties_did_not_join_issue_on_that_case: The parties did not make the unpleaded case an issue for decision in the proceedings.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal involves an appellate reversal based on a case that was neither pleaded nor made an issue between the parties, the appellate judgment is set aside and the trial court’s decree is restored.
